\chapter{Communication Complexity — One Way Minimax}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.CommunicationComplexity.NewmanTheorem.OneWayMinimax
\section{Overview}

This module establishes Yao's minimax principle for one-way public-coin communication
protocols.  It introduces the distributional error of a deterministic one-way protocol
and proves that if every deterministic protocol of cost at most $n$ suffers distributional
error exceeding $\varepsilon$ under some joint input distribution, then the one-way
public-coin communication complexity at error $\varepsilon$ exceeds $n$.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Distributional error of a one-way protocol]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol.distributionalError}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol,
      CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol.run,
      CommunicationComplexity.FiniteProbabilitySpace}
Given a deterministic one-way protocol $p$ computing a function
$f : X \to Y \to \alpha$, and a finite probability distribution $\mu$ on $X \times Y$,
the \emph{distributional error} of $p$ with respect to $\mu$ and $f$ is the real number
\[
  \Pr_{(x,y)\sim\mu}\bigl[p.\mathrm{run}(x,y) \neq f(x,y)\bigr],
\]
i.e.\ the $\mu$-measure of the set of inputs on which the protocol's output disagrees
with $f$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Deterministic protocol from public-coin protocol]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol.toDeterministic}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol,
      CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol}
Given a one-way public-coin protocol $p$ over a randomness space $\Omega$ and a fixed
coin outcome $\omega \in \Omega$, \texttt{toDeterministic}~$p$~$\omega$ is the
deterministic one-way protocol obtained by substituting $\omega$ for the public
randomness: it uses the same message type and sends/decodes by fixing $\omega$ in $p$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Run of derandomised protocol]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol.toDeterministic_run}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol.run,
      CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol,
      CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol.rrun,
      CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol.toDeterministic}
\difficulty{1}
For any public-coin protocol $p$, coin outcome $\omega$, and inputs $x \in X$,
$y \in Y$,
\[
  (p.\mathrm{toDeterministic}(\omega)).\mathrm{run}(x, y)
  \;=\;
  p.\mathrm{rrun}(x, y, \omega).
\]
That is, running the derandomised protocol on $(x,y)$ agrees with running the
randomised protocol on $(x,y)$ with fixed randomness $\omega$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Cost of derandomised protocol]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol.toDeterministic_cost}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol.cost,
      CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol,
      CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol.toDeterministic}
\difficulty{1}
For any public-coin protocol $p$ and coin outcome $\omega$,
\[
  (p.\mathrm{toDeterministic}(\omega)).\mathrm{cost} \;=\; p.\mathrm{cost}.
\]
Fixing the randomness does not change the communication cost of the protocol.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Fubini swap for failure integrals]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.failureIntegral_swap}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.CoinTape,
      CommunicationComplexity.FiniteProbabilitySpace,
      CommunicationComplexity.FiniteProbabilitySpace.measureReal_eq_integral_indicator_one,
      CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol,
      CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol.rrun}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\mu$ be a finite probability measure on $X \times Y$, let $p$ be a one-way
public-coin protocol with coin tape of length $m$, and let $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$.
Then
\[
  \int_{\omega}\Pr_{(x,y)\sim\mu}\bigl[p.\mathrm{rrun}(x,y,\omega)\neq f(x,y)\bigr]\,d\omega
  \;=\;
  \int_{(x,y)\sim\mu}\Pr_{\omega}\bigl[p.\mathrm{rrun}(x,y,\omega)\neq f(x,y)\bigr]\,d\mu,
\]
i.e.\ the order of integration over the coin tape and the input distribution may be
exchanged (Fubini's theorem applied to the $\{0,1\}$-valued failure indicator).
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Yao's minimax principle for one-way protocols]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.lt_communicationComplexity_of_forall_distributionalError_gt}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.CoinTape,
      CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol,
      CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol.cost,
      CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol.distributionalError,
      CommunicationComplexity.FiniteProbabilitySpace,
      CommunicationComplexity.FiniteProbabilitySpace.integral_le_of_le,
      CommunicationComplexity.FiniteProbabilitySpace.lt_integral_of_lt,
      CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol.rrun,
      CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol.toDeterministic,
      CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol.toDeterministic_run,
      CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.communicationComplexity,
      CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.communicationComplexity_le_iff,
      CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.failureIntegral_swap}
\difficulty{5}
Let $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$, $\varepsilon \in \mathbb{R}$, and $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
Suppose there exists a finite joint distribution $\mu$ on $X \times Y$ such that every
deterministic one-way protocol $p$ with $p.\mathrm{cost} \le n$ satisfies
$p.\mathrm{distributionalError}(\mu, f) > \varepsilon$.
Then the one-way public-coin communication complexity of $f$ at error $\varepsilon$
satisfies $n < \mathrm{communicationComplexity}(f, \varepsilon)$.
This is one direction of Yao's minimax principle: a hard input distribution witnesses
a lower bound on randomised complexity.
\end{theorem}
